definition_used: When a journal/publisher/author/third party uses the phrase “legal reasons,” documents litigation or legal threats, or mentions one or more specific laws
caution: Legal reasons are a post-publication transparency signal, not a direct indicator of manuscript content or integrity issues. The definition does not specify what aspect of the article is affected, so problem_object is set to article_general. Actor_context is unclear because the definition mentions multiple possible actors without specifying who invoked the legal reasons.
semantic_rationale: The definition describes a notice or process involving legal reasons, litigation, or laws, which aligns with post-publication transparency and due process oversight. It does not directly indicate issues with research content, authorship, or editorial governance, so only the transparency category is assigned.
